text:
maria: FYI I hit a weird one with the async client — validation errors from the API are turning into a generic ClientError and we lose the JSON body (so no field-level messages).

andrew: can you paste a minimal repro? are you using `httpx` or `aiohttp` under the hood?

maria: async client -> httpx async backend. repro below (super small):
```py
async with RedwoodAsyncClient(api_key=...) as c:
    await c.generate(text='bad-input')  # triggers 422 on our test server
```
stack: `redwood.errors.ClientError: validation failed` with no `.raw_body` or `.details`. response was `application/json` with `errors: [{field: 'prompt', message: 'too long'}]`.

kevin: ugh that sounds like we `.json()`ed and then only surfaced a message string. I think the async path swallows response.content when building the exception to save memory.

priya: this breaks consumers that rely on structured errors for UI form mapping. we should preserve the original body and the parsed errors if available.

maria: opened issue -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/4212 with full trace + test case. tagged `priority/patch` and `sdk/async`. cc @andrew

andrew: saw the issue, thanks. quick Q: do we want to include both `raw_body: Optional[str]` and `parsed_errors: Optional[List[Dict[str,str]]]` on the SDK exception, or a single `payload` blob? typing-wise I'd prefer explicit fields so users don't have to parse.

kevin: explicit fields are nicer, but watch out for breaking changes. we currently expose `ClientError.args[0]` as the message string — can't remove that. adding optional attributes should be safe.

priya: +1 on `raw_body` and `parsed` (maybe `error_details`). make them `Optional[str]` / `Optional[List[Dict[str, str]]]` in types.

andrew: plan: add `raw_body: Optional[str]`, `error_details: Optional[List[Dict[str,str]]]`, and `status_code: Optional[int]` to `RedwoodError` base. keep `.message` for back-compat. I'll add a small adapter for the sync client too so parity between sync/async. will target a minor bump (0.8.x -> 0.9.0 if semver).

maria: sounds good. can you also preserve `content-type` header so we can decide whether to `json.loads`? often we get text/plain with HTML for certain backends and that blows up parsing.

andrew: yes — will include `content_type` in the exception metadata.

kevin: workaround for now: catch `redwood.errors.ClientError` and run `exc.__dict__.get('raw_body') or '<no body>'` — also `httpx.HTTPStatusError` exposes `response.content` so you can fallback to that.

andrew: created draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/4278 with tests for async + sync parity, and a tiny typing change in `exceptions.py`. @maria can you try the branch and validate your repro?

ci-bot: build succeeded for PR 4278 (tox py39, py310) :white_check_mark:

maria: testing now… reproduced locally against the branch — parsed errors appear under `exc.error_details`, and `exc.raw_body` is set. thanks! :tada:

priya: do we want to add a small note in the migration docs about the new fields? some customers might be introspecting exceptions.

andrew: will add a line in CHANGES.md and the exceptions doc page. will also add a short sample in devex examples showing catching the exception and reading `error_details` to map to form fields.

maria: awesome. marking as verified from my side. thank you all. :thumbsup:

andrew: merging after one more review. will cut release tomorrow morning.

kevin: nice, landing this will unblock a few onboarding flows.

maria: closing thread — follow PR for final notes.
